Summary of a fitted model

Source: R/fit.R
summary.baysesp_fit.Rd

Collects in one object what describes a model fitted with baysesp(): the model and its verification mechanism, the priors, the profiles of test results with no verified subject, the convergence diagnostics of the sampler and the posterior summaries of the accuracy of the tests.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'baysesp_fit'
summary(object, level = 0.95, ...)

Arguments

object

A model fitted with baysesp().

level

Probability of the credible intervals in accuracy, a single number in (0, 1). Default 0.95.

...

Not used.

Value

A list of class fit_summary, with a print() method, with the elements:

  • model: a description of the model, such as "log-linear model of order 1".

  • verification: "MAR" or "MNAR", followed by "(one odds ratio per profile)" with by_profile = TRUE.

  • priors: a data frame with the name of each argument that holds a prior (argument) and the prior (prior). The prior on the proportion of diseased in the never-verified profiles has one row per never-verified profile, named after it, such as "unverified_prevalence_prior (0,1)". The priors of the verification mechanism are included when they are used, with the name of the argument of mnar(): "mnar(odds_ratio_prior)" with verification = mnar(), and "mnar(intercepts_prior)" with verification = mnar() in the log-linear and random effects models.

  • never_verified: the never-verified profiles, written as "(0,1)", or a character vector of length 0.

  • diagnostics: a one-row data frame with chains, draws (per chain), backend, max_rhat, min_ess_bulk, min_ess_tail and divergent (number of divergent transitions; NA if not available).

  • accuracy: the result of test_accuracy(), with the odds ratio of verification added under verification = mnar().

  • level: the value of level.

Details

The convergence diagnostics are computed over all the variables saved in the draws (variables that are constant, such as the verified fraction of a never-verified profile, are skipped): the largest split-\(\hat{R}\), which should be below 1.01, the smallest bulk and tail effective sample sizes, which should be at least 100 per chain (Vehtari et al., 2021), and the number of divergent transitions after warmup, which should be 0: divergences mean that the sampler could not explore some region of the posterior, and the draws may be biased.

References

Vehtari, A., Gelman, A., Simpson, D., Carpenter, B. and Bürkner, P.-C. (2021). Rank-normalization, folding, and localization: An improved \(\hat{R}\) for assessing convergence of MCMC (with discussion). Bayesian Analysis, 16(2), 667–718. doi:10.1214/20-BA1221

See also

baysesp(), test_accuracy()

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
d <- simulate_study(n = 1000, prevalence = 0.2,
                    sensitivity = c(A = 0.9, B = 0.8),
                    specificity = c(A = 0.85, B = 0.95),
                    verification_prob = c(0.2, 0.9, 0.9, 1))
d <- baysesp_data(d, tests = c("A", "B"), verified = "verified", disease = "disease")
fit <- baysesp(d, seed = 1)
summary(fit)
#> Model:          saturated model, transparent parametrization
#> Verification:   MAR
#> Never verified: none
#> 
#> Priors:
#>   frequency_prior           Dirichlet(concentration = 1)
#>   verified_prior            Beta(mean = 0.5, precision = 2)
#>   profile_prevalence_prior  Beta(mean = 0.5, precision = 1)
#> 
#> Sampling: 4 chains x 1000 draws (rstan)
#>   max R-hat 1.003, min bulk ESS 2426, min tail ESS 989, divergent transitions 0
#> 
#> Accuracy (95% credible intervals):
#>    quantity  mean median lower upper identified
#>  prevalence 0.203  0.203 0.178 0.230       TRUE
#>       Se[A] 0.895  0.897 0.841 0.937       TRUE
#>       Sp[A] 0.850  0.850 0.824 0.875       TRUE
#>      PPV[A] 0.603  0.603 0.545 0.660       TRUE
#>      NPV[A] 0.969  0.970 0.951 0.982       TRUE
#>       Se[B] 0.798  0.799 0.733 0.855       TRUE
#>       Sp[B] 0.947  0.947 0.930 0.962       TRUE
#>      PPV[B] 0.794  0.795 0.735 0.848       TRUE
#>      NPV[B] 0.948  0.949 0.929 0.964       TRUE
# }
